related_questions.question: What is the most accurate COVID test?

text_blocks.snippet: The PCR test is the most accurate COVID-19 test available. PCR tests detect the virus's genetic material (RNA) and are highly sensitive and specific. While other tests like antigen tests are also available, they are less sensitive and may not detect the virus as reliably, especially in individuals with low viral loads.

list.title: PCR Tests:
list.snippet: These tests are performed in a laboratory and are considered the gold standard for COVID-19 testing due to their high accuracy.

list.title: Antigen Tests:
list.snippet: While faster and more convenient, antigen tests are less sensitive than PCR tests and may produce false negative results, especially in individuals with early or asymptomatic infections.

list.title: Factors Affecting Accuracy:
list.snippet: The accuracy of any COVID-19 test can also be affected by factors like the timing of the test, the type of sample taken, and the specific variant of the virus.

related_questions.question: How to test for COVID at home?

text_blocks.snippet: To test for COVID-19 at home, use an over-the-counter (OTC) rapid antigen test. Follow the specific instructions included with your test kit, as they may vary. Generally, this involves collecting a nasal sample with a swab, mixing it with a solution, and applying drops to a test strip. Read the results based on the control and test lines appearing on the strip. If the control line is missing, the test is invalid and should be repeated. A positive result, indicated by a line on the test line, means you likely have COVID-19. A negative result, indicated by only the control line, may require retesting, especially if symptoms are present.
snippet_highlighted_words: use an over-the-counter (OTC) rapid antigen test

list.title: 1. Gather your materials:
list.snippet: You'll need the OTC COVID-19 rapid antigen test kit and a timer.

list.title: 2. Prepare the test:
list.snippet: Read the manufacturer's instructions carefully, as procedures can vary. Some tests require a specific number of swab rotations in the solution.

list.title: 3. Collect the sample:
list.snippet: Follow the instructions on how to collect your nasal sample. This typically involves inserting a swab into one nostril and rotating it several times.

list.title: 4. Process the sample:
list.snippet: Combine the swab with the provided solution and follow the instructions for mixing.

list.title: 5. Apply the sample:
list.snippet: Put the designated number of drops onto the test strip and start the timer.

list.title: 6. Read the results:
list.snippet: Check the test strip after the specified time. If a control line appears, the test is valid. A line on the test line indicates a positive result, meaning you likely have COVID-19. If only the control line appears, the result is negative. A negative result may need to be retested, especially if you have symptoms.

list.title: 7. Dispose of the test:
list.snippet: Follow the instructions for proper disposal of the used test.

list.title: 8. Report your results:
list.snippet: Some testing programs encourage reporting results, even if negative, to help track the spread of the virus.
